main_text.l: Mente simul iubet invocari Securiore : ut candida quæ tuis Semper relucet pollicitis fides, Hæc dicta firmet. Namque cuncta Sancte Deus potiore præstas. Promissa nutu. Nunc igitur tui Domum Davidis sollicitus vide Vultu benigno : splendidisque Auxiliis columnem tuere. Sic illa veris tuta favoribus Florens per urbes vivet Isacidum. Huic (te sereno) nulla posthac Sæcla ferent moribunda finem.

CÆLO tonantis dextera Numinis Fastus superbos quum Babyloniæ, Cunctisque formidata regna Contudit: Atque trucem Tyrannū, (Qui sancta templi vasa Syonii Servire mensis iusserat ebriis, Sacrosque Iacobi cruentis Presserat Imperiis nepotes,) Fervente tandem Medus acynace

page.notes: The woodcut divider between the verse and the title is ornament, not text. The drop cap C is decorative and is joined to the first word as CÆLO. "Feruente" is read as "fervente" by the u/v rule. Doubtful: "Tyrannū" (tilde reading), "acynace" (final letter), and the letter after "Hæc", which may be "ac" without ligature. Printing errors are left as printed.
